newsitem.title: USA: Molten Metal named in shareholder lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Molten Metal named in shareholder lawsuit.

text.p: Molten Metal Technology Inc was named in a suit requesting class action status alleging the company misrepresented information about the nature of Molten's waste processing technology, commercial ventures and its relationship with the U.S. Department of Energy, lawyers for the plaintiffs said Wednesday.

The suit was filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts on behalf of those who bought Molten shares between September 26, 1995, and October 21, 1996, said plaintiffs' lawfirm Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP.
A Molten spokeswoman said the company was drawing up a response to the suit but could not immediately comment.

The suit alleges that Molten mischaracterized the nature of the company's technology, and knew, but did not disclose, serious problems with the development of its molten metal technology and that continued Department of Energy funding for that technology was in serious jeopardy, a statement issued by Milberg Weiss said.

The suit says that when defendants finally revealed the Department of Energy had terminated or substantially reduced future funding for Molten Metal and certain commercial ventures would be canceled or postponed, the price of Molten Metal common stock declined in one day by 49 percent, or $13-7/8 per share, to close at only $14-1/4 per share.

Before any such disclosures were made however, the complaint alleges that the seven officers and directors named as defendants sold in excess of 450,000 shares of Molten Metal stock they personally held, at prices as high as $38 per share, for proceeds in excess of $15,350,000.
"The damages are substantial but it remains to be seen just how much they are," said Jerome Congress, the Milberg Weiss lawyer on the case.
Molten Metal said in a statement released later Wednesday that it believes the lawsuit "is completely without merit" and it "intends to contest the suit vigorously."
